newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen down 30-40 bcf in wkly AGAs.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen down 30-40 bcf in wkly AGAs.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to fall by 30-40 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said this week.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for a drawdown ranged widely from 20 bcf to 54 bcf for the week ended March 28.

"The consuming area is going to have a pretty sizeable draw. The LDCs (local distribution companies) need to get that gas out of there before the injection season. We may see an increase in the producing region though," one source said.

In last report, overall stocks fell by 54 bcf, above expectations, and were still 207 bcf above year-ago. Eastern storage last week pared its gain over year-ago levels again to 189 bcf. The four week average draw is 58 bcf.

For the same week last year, total inventories dropped by 51 bcf, meaning a draw today in the expected range would boost the overall surplus to 1996 to about 223 bcf. Eastern storage fell by 35 bcf last year, while producing stocks dropped by 10 bcf and western stocks were up down six bcf.
Many traders said next week's report will likely have more impact on the market since it will show the first evidence of the spring injection season.
